relevance_note: Single-patient case report of Alexander disease with a GFAP variant: "Genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous point mutation in exon 6 of the GFAP gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON from values I chose (no table transcription; the paper has no tables). In scope: the case-report patient (label 'patient'); his two parents, who were tested and found negative ('parent of patient', 'parent of patient 2'; sex not given individually); and two previously published people from the Discussion with individual-level facts: the Nam et al., 2015 patient (E312ter, headache, short-term memory disturbances, adult onset) and the boy described by Alexander, 1949 (16-month-old, megalencephaly, hydrocephalus, psychomotor regression; no variant given, so no variant row). The Nam features are stated about 'This E312ter mutation' rather than about a named person; the text later calls the two E312 carriers 'these two patients', so I attributed them to that one patient. Patient onset recorded as 'age five months' (age when he 'seemed healthy until' and was referred for developmental delay); no age at diagnosis is stated. Vital status left not reported (last follow-up at ten years, no explicit statement). Variant: no cDNA, transcript or genomic coordinates printed; only 'guanine-to-adenine change' in exon 6 and Glu312Lys (E312K). 'missence' (sic) in the Discussion gives the variant type. In-silico predictions (SIFT, PolyPhen-2, Mutation Taster, MUpro) are not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is not reported. De novo: both parents tested negative; the authors add that germline mosaicism remained possible. Checklist choices: microcephaly does not exclude the broader 'macrocephaly or megalencephaly' item (left not reported); enlarged ventricles with atrophy not mapped to hydrocephalus; 'brain stem was diffusely small' not mapped to medulla/cervical cord (medulla not named); internal/external capsule signal not mapped to basal ganglia; poor responsiveness not mapped to cognitive decline; 'would not track objects visually' not mapped to eye movement abnormality. Normal findings not recorded as specific exclusions because they name nothing specific: 'vital signs were all normal', 'The remainder of the physical examination was normal', normal newborn screen, and negative tests for other leukodystrophies (differential diagnoses). Upper-limb tone and reflexes were normal at five months but tone later became diffusely increased and reflexes difficult to elicit; recorded as time-specific rows, not a contradiction. Family history negative for close relatives with neurological disorders is not attributed to the parents individually (group not named).
